Studydown

Support

Straightforward help for face-down timing, plans, purchase restoration, and your files.

Common questions

How do I start a focus session?

Choose or create an Activity, start the timer, and place the iPhone flat and still with its screen facing down. Studydown starts recording after it detects that position.

Why did the timer not start?

Make sure the iPhone is nearly flat, still, and Studydown is active. A steep angle or ongoing movement can prevent face-down detection.

Free: 3 Activities, 5 minutes

Keep up to 3 Activities and 300 seconds (5 minutes) of total recorded time, with Today and This Week summaries and basic CSV. This is not a daily allowance. Lifetime Pro removes both limits; a face-down session already underway is saved without trimming.

Lifetime Pro

A single lifetime unlock adds unlimited Activities, month, year, and custom analysis, weekly goals, Deadlines, Apple Watch, Widgets, advanced hero styles, and complete JSON backup and restore. No subscription.

How do I restore Lifetime Pro?

Open the Lifetime Pro screen and choose Restore Purchases while signed in to the Apple Account used for the purchase. Apple verifies the entitlement.

How do CSV and JSON files differ?

Basic CSV is available free for tabular records. Lifetime Pro adds a complete JSON backup and restore. A file is created only when you request it and goes to a destination you choose.

How can I check a short session?

In Settings, set Shortest session to keep to 3 seconds. Choose an Activity, tap Start timing, and keep the iPhone still and face down for at least 10 seconds after detection. Keep Studydown active and the phone unlocked. Lift it and end the session or let the grace period expire. Sessions shorter than your chosen minimum are discarded.

How do I change reminders?

In Settings, turn reminders on or off and choose a daily time or an interval of 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, or 12 hours. Notifications require permission, but declining them does not prevent timing. Locking the phone or leaving the app stops active time accumulation; iOS can still deliver scheduled reminders.
